clue.text: See 10
Penny coming in dispatches fritters?

indicators.note: one thing coming in to another enters it, so the coin goes inside the other word

parts.note: to dispatch is to send off
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A question of whether a penny arriving with the post gets frittered away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fritters' looks like a plural noun (fried batter) but is the verb: someone fritters money away, i.e. SPENDS it.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money is to waste it in small amounts, a loose synonym for spending it.

clue.text: Locus of scandal: criminal scope of it carrying force

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it inside, so the jumble holds the extra letter
something criminal is crooked, so the letters that follow are bent out of their order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A news-style line about the scene of a scandal, with criminal reach being forced through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole puzzle is themed on the Horizon IT scandal, in which the UK Post Office wrongly prosecuted hundreds of sub-postmasters; 3 is cross-referenced throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: The British Post Office was the institution at the centre of the Horizon miscarriage-of-justice scandal.

clue.text: Kajagoogoo singer in Peruvian city hotel on lake

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
L is the abbreviation for lake, placed after the rest

explanation.surface: A 1980s pop singer is pictured staying at a lakeside hotel in Peru.
explanation.walkthrough: Limahl, whose stage name is an anagram of his surname Hamill, fronted the band Kajagoogoo ('Too Shy').
explanation.definitionFit: Limahl was the lead vocalist of the 1980s British pop group Kajagoogoo.

clue.text: Male, in truth, that is insincerely suave sort

indicators.note: a letter placed in a word sits inside it, so the male letter goes within the old word for truth

parts.note: sooth is an archaic word for truth, as in soothsayer
M is the abbreviation for male
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A man who, truth be told, is a slick and insincere charmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is informal for a man with a polished, ingratiating manner that is not quite sincere.

clue.text: Mate has 3 going in both directions

indicators.note: travelling both ways means the item is written once backwards and once forwards

parts.note: the answer to 3, abbreviated to its initials, taken one way
the same initials taken the other way

explanation.surface: A friend is credited with having the cross-referenced item heading two ways at once.
explanation.walkthrough: PO, the abbreviation of the answer to 3, appears twice: first back to front, then the right way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a colleague or friend, from 'opposite number'.

clue.text: From Yank it's a sound prize?

indicators.note: a sound is something heard, so the words are to be spoken and listened to

parts.note: to yank is to pull, so 'yank it's' becomes 'pull it's' when said

explanation.surface: An American is asked whether a prize is a sound one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From Yank' also hints that the prize is American, and the American pronunciation PULL-it-ser matches 'pull it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pulitzer is an American award for journalism, literature and music, so it is a prize.

clue.text: Man distressed by treacherous woman?

parts.note: surface reading: any man upset by a two-timing partner
setter's reading: dis-tressed, literally deprived of his tresses by a betrayer, as in the Bible story of Delilah

explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' splits as dis-tressed: the biblical strongman lost his strength when Delilah had his hair cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: In Judges, the strongman's betrayer Delilah had his hair shorn, taking away his strength.

clue.text: Instrument you fake for broadcast? I'm not sure

indicators.note: something meant for broadcast is heard rather than read, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a fake is a phoney, and 'you phoney' said quickly gives the opening sounds
um is the noise of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone accuses another of faking an instrument for radio, then hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: The euphonium is a brass instrument, a tenor tuba used in brass and military bands.

clue.text: CEO returning award, remorseful at last: annul please — very dodgy

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or crooked, so the collected letters are scrambled
at last points to the final letter of the preceding word only

parts.note: the final letter of remorseful
taken as written for the mix
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A boss handing back an honour, finally sorry, pleads to have it annulled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very dodgy' reads as a comment, but very supplies a letter and dodgy stirs the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Paula Vennells, Post Office chief executive during the Horizon prosecutions, handed back her CBE in 2024 amid public outrage.

clue.text: Joke found in New Testament work

indicators.note: something found in another is located inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: NT is the standard abbreviation for New Testament
a joke is 'the one about...', as in 'have you heard the one'

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have spotted a joke inside the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a musical composition for nine performers, so it is a work.

clue.text: Game in long time one must stop: these from 3 not enough!

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it, so the sport sits within the period
a stopper plugs a gap, so the one is pushed in as a plug

parts.note: ages is an informal long time
polo is a game played on horseback
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A long-running game, and the institution's expressions of regret are judged not enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions happen at different points: 'in' places the game near the start of the long time, and 'stop' plugs the one further along.
explanation.definitionFit: The Post Office's apologies to wrongly convicted sub-postmasters were widely criticised as inadequate.

clue.text: Salacious but quiet amid endless calm

indicators.note: without an end means the last letter of the word for calm is dropped
amid means in the middle of, so the quiet word goes inside

parts.note: a lull is a calm spell, cut short
STFU is the crude internet abbreviation for 'shut the f*** up', a demand for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone is lustful but outwardly quiet in a calm setting.
explanation.walkthrough: The rude STFU is fittingly hidden inside a word meaning salacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Salacious means having or showing excessive sexual interest, which is to be full of lust.

clue.text: Faulty 3 system as far as one can see?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Fujitsu accounting software at the Post Office whose bugs caused false shortfalls

definitions.text: as far as one can see
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the line where earth meets sky, the limit of vision

explanation.walkthrough: The faulty software's name is an ordinary word for the edge of the visible world.
explanation.definitionFit: The Post Office's flawed IT system was called Horizon, and the horizon is the furthest line visible to an observer.

clue.text: Athlete on mountain eating a vegetable

parts.note: a runner is an athlete

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so the mountain swallows the letter

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner on a mountain is snacking on vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner bean is a climbing bean whose long green pods are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Son with us greeting Japanese dish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A son joins the family and says hello over a Japanese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is the Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish and other toppings.

clue.text: Derides old Fujitsu leader twice with glass shattered

indicators.note: shattered glass is broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of glass broken up
O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, taken two times over

parts.note: the opening letter of Fujitsu
the opening letter again

explanation.surface: Critics deride the former Fujitsu boss as things lie in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Fujitsu built the faulty Horizon system; 'slag off' is British slang for criticising harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To slag off is British slang for insulting or rubbishing someone, a colloquial synonym for derides.

clue.text: Problems in electronics for starters causing confusion

indicators.note: starters are the opening items, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Faults in electronic gear lead to chaos, a nod to the buggy Horizon system.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie (or pi) is a printing term for type that has been jumbled together.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, pie is a jumbled mass of spilt type, hence a state of confusion or disorder.

clue.text: Exploitative body PO duplicitous with trader?

indicators.note: a duplicitous party is deceptive and twisted, so the letters are twisted round

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Post Office is cast as an exploitative organisation dealing deceitfully with a trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator is one that preys on others, so an exploitative person or organisation.

clue.text: Welshwoman English track among Poles

indicators.note: something among others is surrounded by them, so the pair goes between the poles

parts.note: N and S, the north and south poles
E is the abbreviation for English
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A woman from Wales is placed on an English railway line among Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the people of Poland; it is the two ends of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerys is a Welsh girl's name, so a woman bearing it is typically Welsh.

clue.text: Jocks found in hammock among the crew?

indicators.note: something among others sits in their midst, so the bed goes inside the crew

parts.note: SS is a steamship, and its men are the crew
a cot is a naval hammock-style hanging bed

explanation.surface: Scottish sailors are discovered asleep in their hammocks aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jock is informal, sometimes derogatory, British slang for a Scotsman, so Jocks are Scotsmen.

clue.text: Ogle cheery magazine exposing 3 scandal

definitions.note: a verb defining a noun: to ogle is to give the glad eye

parts.note: glad means happy
Private Eye, the satirical magazine that reported the Horizon scandal for years

explanation.surface: Readers ogle a cheery magazine that broke the Post Office story.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical and investigative fortnightly, often called just the Eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The glad eye is an amorous or inviting look, so giving it amounts to ogling someone.

clue.text: Willing to finish early — scrap strategic move

indicators.note: finishing early means stopping before the last letter, so the final one is lost

parts.note: game means willing, cut short
a bit is a scrap

explanation.surface: Someone ready to wrap up early by dropping a tactic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move in chess that sacrifices material, hence any calculated strategic ploy.

clue.text: Composer at sea left band without piano backing

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the musical letter for soft is dropped
backing means going backwards, so the combined letters are read right to left

parts.note: port is the nautical left, minus P for piano
a seam is a band of mineral in rock

explanation.surface: A composer at sea abandons his band and gets no piano accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like an anagram signal, but it points to the sailor's word for left; P is the musical marking piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is an honorific for a distinguished composer or conductor, a master of music.

clue.text: Sub-postmaster against 3 in film sat happily with beer

parts.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture

indicators.note: a happy-go-lucky arrangement is a loose one, so these letters are freely reordered

parts.note: taken as written for the mix
taken as written for the mix

explanation.surface: The hero of a TV drama about the scandal is pictured relaxing contentedly over a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in film' suggests the ITV drama, but film is wordplay. Alan Bates led the sub-postmasters' fight; the drama is called 'Mr Bates vs The Post Office'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bates, the sub-postmaster who led the campaign, is the 'Mr Bates' of the drama's title, fighting the Post Office.

clue.text: Bird closed beak on morsel

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
bit, past tense of bite: closed one's jaws on something

explanation.surface: A bird snaps its beak shut on a tasty scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A titbit is a small, tasty piece of food, so it is a morsel.

clue.text: One in the wind, singular events involving 3 staff?

indicators.note: one placed in something is put inside it, so the numeral goes within the wind's name

parts.note: the mistral is a strong cold wind of southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone caught in the wind witnesses unusual events involving Post Office employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like it means odd; it supplies its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Many sub-postmasters' prosecutions were unsafe, trials ruined by unreliable Horizon evidence, so they were mistrials.

clue.text: Have novel experience with 10 1's successor?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to get through a book, a novel
second meaning: Nick ___, a later chief executive of the Post Office

explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like 'new'; it is a book. Nick Read became Post Office chief executive after Paula Vennells' departure.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading a novel is experiencing it, and Nick Read later succeeded to the Post Office's top job.

clue.text: See 22
Lacking energy conclude article further on

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for energy is removed

parts.note: to infer is to conclude, minus E for energy
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A tired person decides the item should come later.
explanation.walkthrough: Infra is Latin, used in texts as 'see infra', meaning see below.
explanation.definitionFit: Infra is a Latin word used in footnotes to send the reader below or later in the text.

clue.text: Backing musical about 3 worker

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the whole string is read from its end

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
re means about or concerning
the initials of the answer to 3

explanation.surface: Supporting a stage show about the Post Office employee.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker, especially a skilled factory hand or a secret agent.
